title: Service sculpting, priority shims, and noisy-neighbor rules
content:
Context:

This is a working note for an operationally simple but flexible pattern to protect higher-tier customers from noisy tenants while preserving global capacity and enabling regional failover. Goal is to define a set of lightweight primitives (service sculpting, priority shims, admission gates) that the control plane can evaluate cheaply at the edge and the global router can enforce across regions.

Why this: we've seen two recurring operational pain points:
- sudden large-burst tenants (model training/ad-hoc batch jobs) saturate a few pools and push up latencies for paid customers in the same region.
- cross-region disruptions where naive failover floods a second region and causes cascading throttles.

Design principles / constraints:
- decisions should be made with cheap signals at the router (no full policy evaluation per token)
- allow deterministic precedence: contract SLA > reserved capacity > dynamic priority > best-effort
- soft-degradation preferred over hard rejects for customer experience (graceful fallback models, slower paths)
- must support multi-region routing: preference ordering, burst isolation, and backpressure propagation
- runtime must be audit-friendly and observable (traceable decision reasons)

Primitive definitions (naming intentionally distinct from existing docs):
1) Service sculpting
   - short, declarative per-tenant profile that previews how traffic is allowed to flow: reserved_slots, burst_budget, allowed_regions, preferred_regions, fallback_models
   - stored in control plane repo as a small JSON blob per tenant (versioned, pinned by contract)
   - evaluated at edge to decide initial routing and to calculate per-request admission weight

2) Priority shims
   - a lightweight numeric priority added to requests: base_priority + contract_override + dynamic_elevations
   - used only for ordering among contenders during admission when capacity constrained
   - priority ranges documented: [1000..1999] reserved/enterprise, [500..999] paid, [1..499] free/experimental

3) Admission gates (fast checks at router edge)
   - token_quota_check (per-minute token allowance vs aggregated usage)
   - concurrent_streams_check (max concurrent requests per tenant per region)
   - burst_budget_check (consume/restore budget atomically; if empty, drop into degraded path)
   - policy cache TTL: 5s for fast-changing tenants, 60s for stable accounts

4) Service shims (degraded paths)
   - model-fallback shim: redirect to lower-cost/quantized model variant with loss-tolerance policies
   - slow-path shim: accept but place into a longer tail queue with explicit SLO bounds
   - partial-response shim: stream tokens up to soft limit then return truncated output with indicator

Noisy neighbor detection heuristics (signals we can compute cheaply):
- token rate per-tenant relative to historical median (5x increase over 1–5m window triggers alert)
- burst_count: number of large requests (>10k tokens) in sliding 15m window
- queue-growth: region queue depth where tenant accounts for >20% of inflight queued work for 2m+
- repeated evictions: tenant hit >N admission gates in a day

Enforcement strategy (how decisions are applied):
- admission gates run in the edge router. If request passes, it is scored and routed. If it fails, we attempt service shims in-order: (1) model-fallback, (2) slow-path, (3) reject
- routing includes region preference + capacity probe: pick preferred region if its free capacity > headroom_threshold else try next allowed region
- backpressure propagation: region returns a backpressure signal to control plane with reason codes (LATENCY_HIGH, POOL_FULL, EVICTIONS_HIGH). Control plane increments tenant's dynamic_elevation negative factor to reduce priority temporarily

Multi-region considerations:
- regional headroom is primary signal for failover. Headroom computed as free_gpu_slots - reserved_slots - soft_buffer(%)
- failover window damping: if a tenant fails over from R1->R2, mark tenant in R2 with a temporary lower burst_budget for 10 minutes to avoid ripples
- global token budgets: tenants have a global daily token cap; region-level quotas enforce local fairness
- cross-region routing rule: prefer same-region unless headroom < 15% or latency penalty of fallback_models > acceptable_delta

Quota model sketch (cheap to evaluate):
- three layers: contract_reserved (hard guarantee), daily_committed (soft daily rhythm), on_call_shares (best-effort burstable)
- counters are stored in globally sharded fast-store with per-region mirrors; reconciliation run asynchronously to correct drift
- local admission checks use approximate counters (sketches) to reduce RPCs; violations flagged for audit rather than immediate hard-rejects except for contract_reserved

Observability & debugging surface:
- every admit decision emits a small reason tuple: (tenant_id, admit_result, reason_code, priority_value, region_chosen, policy_version)
- dashboard: tenant heatmap (token-rate, burst-budget, admitted %, shims used) and region impact matrix
- traces: on elevated incidents, link trace ids (router -> control-plane -> pool) and include last 3 policy versions applied

Rollout plan (safe, incremental):
1) Canary gates in staging for 2 tenants (non-critical) with full telemetry enabled
2) Shadow mode in prod: evaluate gates but always pass; collect decision telemetry for 1 week
3) Soft-enforce: enable service shims only (no hard rejects) for small subset of paid customers
4) Full enforcement for subset of regions with manual ops on-call
5) Global rollout after 4 weeks of stable signals and resolved issues

Operational runbook snippets (for SRE/ops):
- If region reports POOL_FULL and cascade risk, temporarily raise soft_buffer to 20% and enable slow-path shim globally for free tier
- If a tenant is repeatedly hitting admission gates: contact SE for account discussion; optionally move to dedicated pool or increase reserved_slots
- Revoke burst_budget for tenants with abuse patterns (automated policy after 3 strikes in 24h) and flag for sales follow-up

Open questions / trade-offs (to decide):
- exact numerical boundaries for priority buckets and tuning knobs (we should A/B these with traffic)
- how aggressive the control plane should be about reducing priority on backpressure signals (instant vs windowed)
- data consistency model for counters (exact vs approximate) — currently leaning approximate with audit reconciliation

Immediate action items (owners):
- Arjun: prototype admission gate SDK in edge router (P0) — due 2025-11-07
- Liam: dashboard mockups + telemetry schema (include reason tuple) — due 2025-11-14
- Maya: draft policy JSON schema and versioning rules, add Confluence page — due 2025-10-17

Notes / stray ideas (brainstorm):
- allow tenants to opt-in to cooperative burst pools (shared budget across tenants who agree to preemption rules)
- per-model cost weights baked into admission scoring so heavy models get penalized when tight
- runtime feature: short-circuit KV-cache hits to preserve low-latency requests even under high token churn

References and related tickets: see linked_artifacts for the initial implementation RFC, PLAT-789 for backlog, and PR #1324 in runtime for priority field plumbing.

— end of working note —

(thumbnotes: this is intentionally pedestrian and focused on quick wins operators can implement without large infra rebuilds. We can later converge these primitives into the policy language if we decide to support richer evals.)
